anthropic.grade: A (S-1/A) for 2026; C for commitments after the next 12 months; D for opex outside compute
anthropic.note: Q3 revenue $17.0B × 4. Compute run-rate $25.1B (Q3 × 4), 64–74% training, research and internal use. Commitments: $69.8B due Oct 2026–Sep 2027 (A), $447.5B through 2030 (C, via secondary reading of the S-1/A), so ≈$116B a year after that (D). Opex outside compute ≈$17B a year from H1 2026 sales and marketing, G&A and R&D staff (D), grown 1.5× a year.

openai.note: Press reports of OpenAI’s own investor projections (The Information, FT), revised three times in 2026. Revenue 2026 $36B and 2027 $62B; training compute $32B and $65B; free cash flow −$25B, −$57B, −$85B, −$51B for 2026–29, positive in 2030. The $122B March raise includes $35B of Amazon money on conditions. The next round’s target was cut from $30B to $20B (FT, late Oct).

pools.private_note: CB Insights AI venture funding. Without OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s mega-rounds the quarters are ≈$117B, $88B and $103B: no clear trend.

capacity.note: What OpenAI and Anthropic could raise: a 30–40% share (they took ≈38% in Jan–Sep 2026) of private AI funding at its Q3 pace ($103B a quarter), shrinking 20% or growing 30% a year. Sovereign money and hyperscaler stakes arrive inside these rounds. D.

pools.hyperscaler: Free cash flow is about zero: Amazon −$42B over the last 12 months, Alphabet −$9B in Q3, Meta −$2B in Q3, Oracle −$5B; Microsoft +$19B. Hyperscalers still fund labs with equity and credits, but those are now paid for with debt.
pools.debt: AI-related debt: $322B in 2025, $489B in 2026 to July 22 (Goldman). It is getting dearer: bond books ≈5× → ≈2× covered; Oracle cut to BBB−, 5-year CDS ≈128 → 295bp; CoreWeave 2031 unsecured bonds yield >16%.

signals.t: OpenAI cut its round target from $30B to $20B and its valuation target from ≈$1.4T to $1.25T.
Anthropic’s IPO valuation talk is ≈$1.5T, down from ≈$2T.
Labs are moving compute from pre-training to RL.
No hyperscaler has cut 2026 capex guidance; that would be the next signal.
